newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil - low sulphur lower on good supplies.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil - low sulphur lower on good supplies.

text.p: NWE fuel oil slipped on Wednesday as very thin activity pressured prices lower.
Slower bunker demand leant on barge numbers with deals this morning at $117 a tonne fob ARA, about $1 off Tuesday's levels.
"I don't expect there to be much volume now before the Christmas break," said one barge trader.
The recent strong demand from shippers looking for material ahead of the holiday period now seems to have been met.
High sulphur cargoes were a touch lower essentially taking into account weaker barges. Dealers saw little interest.
"Enquiries seem to be limited to tidying up and balancing stocks," said one.

Low sulphur was knocked lower on good supplies meeting muted demand. A 25,000 tonne cargo was sold this morning at $126.75 fob NWE. The cargo, loading at the end of December is understood to be heading into the Mediterranean to cover a short.
Four cargoes, one of 45-50kt, remain available for Dec early Jan loading and there were no obvious buyers.
"I think the market is heading down which will open the way to take material to the U.S," said one trader at a major.
